chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sees in a dream until he experiences desire, and he thinks that he has had a wet dream; then when he wakes up, he does not see any fluid on his garment nor on his body. He said: Ghusl is not obligatory upon him. And he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: Ghusl is only due from the major fluid; so if he sees something in his dream and does not see the major fluid, then no ghusl is obligatory upon him.

key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: to have had a wet dream
key_terms.الشَّهْوَةَ: sexual desire experienced in the dream
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath that becomes obligatory in certain states of janabah
key_terms.الْمَاءَ الْأَكْبَرِ: the major fluid that necessitates ghusl
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: sleep or dreaming state in which the incident is seen

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl obligatory if someone feels sexual desire in a dream but finds no discharge upon waking?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ghusl after a dream involving sexual desire. It states that ghusl becomes obligatory only when the major fluid is actually found, not merely because one thought he had experienced ihtilam in sleep.
